sentiment.label: risk_off
sentiment.reason_it: Il sentiment di mercato è risk-off a causa dell'aumento del VIX (+6.78%) e della chiusura negativa dei mercati azionari (S&P 500 -1.24%). Il DXY è salito (+0.39%) e il TLT è sceso (-1.48%), segnalando una maggiore avversione al rischio. L'inflazione globale e le tensioni geopolitiche continuano a pesare sui mercati.
sentiment.reason_en: Market sentiment is risk-off due to the increase in VIX (+6.78%) and the negative close of equity markets (S&P 500 -1.24%). The DXY rose (+0.39%) and TLT fell (-1.48%), indicating increased risk aversion. Global inflation and geopolitical tensions continue to weigh on markets.

market_impact_summary.it: I mercati azionari sono chiusi per il weekend. Nella chiusura precedente, S&P 500 ha perso l'1.24%. Il VIX è salito a 18.43. Il DXY è avanzato (+0.39%) e il TLT è sceso (-1.48%). L'oro è sceso (-2.48%) e il petrolio è salito (+3.35%).
market_impact_summary.en: Equity markets are closed for the weekend. In the previous close, S&P 500 lost 1.24%. VIX rose to 18.43. DXY advanced (+0.39%) and TLT fell (-1.48%). Gold declined (-2.48%) and oil rose (+3.35%).

audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Mentre le borse mondiali osservano la consueta pausa festiva, i riflettori restano accesi sul comparto digitale che opera 24 ore su 24

Nella seduta di nella seduta precedente, il Nikkei ha chiuso in calo dell'1.99%, Shanghai in calo dell'1.02%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura debole per i mercati europei se fossero aperti.

Sul fronte occidentale, nella seduta di nella seduta precedente, S&P 500 in calo dell'1.24%, VIX in rialzo del 6.78%, DXY in rialzo dello 0.39%. L'oro è sceso a $4561.9/oncia, in calo del 2.48%. Il petrolio invece ha guadagnato il 3.35% a $109.26

In campo geopolitico, i titoli di stato globali sono stati colpiti dalle preoccupazioni per uno shock inflazionistico derivante dal conflitto in Iran. Intanto, la Cina e gli USA stanno discutendo possibili accordi commerciali.

Nessun dato macro rilevante in uscita oggi.

Passando agli asset digitali, Bitcoin quota $78,119 con una variazione del -0.02%. Il sentiment è risk-off.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin si mantiene sopra i settantottomila dollari, con una variazione del -0,26% nella giornata di oggi. Gli ETF su Bitcoin hanno registrato un deflusso netto di 290,4 milioni di dollari. Questo movimento potrebbe essere influenzato dalle recenti dinamiche di mercato e dagli sviluppi normativi. Inoltre, gli analisti di Santiment segnalano un aumento dell'euforia su Bitcoin grazie al CLARITY Act statunitense. 
  Sul fronte delle altcoin, Ethereum scambia a duemiladuecentottantasei dollari, con un calo dello 0,42%, mentre Solana è a ottantasette dollari, in ribasso dello 0,54%. BNB viene scambiato a seicentocinquantacinque dollari, con una flessione dello 0,89%. 
  Il Fear & Greed Index è a 27, in zona Fear, suggerisce cautela sugli investitori.

Sui mercati attendiamo i dati economici in uscita oggi. Per approfondire i temi di oggi, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en:
Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. 

While global stock markets are observing their usual festive pause, the spotlight remains on the digital sector, which operates 24/7

In the previous session, the Nikkei closed down 1.99%, Shanghai down 1.02%. This suggests a weak opening for European markets if they were open.

On the Western front, in the previous session, S&P 500 down 1.24%, VIX up 6.78%, DXY up 0.39%. Gold fell to $4561.9/oz, down 2.48%. Oil instead gained 3.35% to $109.26

In the geopolitical field, global government bonds were hit by concerns over an inflationary shock deriving from the conflict in Iran. Meanwhile, China and the US are discussing possible trade agreements.

No relevant macroeconomic data out today.

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets... Bitcoin is quoted at $78,119 with a variation of -0.02%. The sentiment is risk-off.

Bitcoin is holding above seventy-eight thousand dollars, with a variation of -0.26% today. Bitcoin ETFs have recorded a net outflow of $290.4 million. This movement could be influenced by recent market dynamics and regulatory developments. Additionally, Santiment analysts report an increase in euphoria on Bitcoin thanks to the CLARITY Act in the US. 

On the altcoin front, Ethereum trades at $2,286, down 0.42%, while Solana is at $87, down 0.54%. BNB is traded at $655, with a decline of 0.89%. 

The Fear & Greed Index is at 27, in Fear zone, suggesting caution among investors.

We are waiting for economic data out today. To delve deeper into today's themes, find the full articles in the Top Stories section on our platform. Thanks for your attention and see you tomorrow.

articles.title: How to Win a Trade War: Book launch and discussion with Bown and Keynes
articles.snippet: Soumaya Keynes and Chad P. Bown discuss their new book How to Win a Trade War, available for pre-order. Trade wars are here to stay, and refusing to engage in the fight is no longer an option. President Donald Trump's tariff announcements can crash markets and sour decades-long alliances. China's export restrictions on rare earths could bring the West's car production to a crashing halt. Curbs on trade in cutting-edge chips could determine who wins the artificial intelligence (AI) race. From identifying supply chain vulnerabilities to installing stockpiles, subsidies, and trade restrictions,…

articles.summary_en: The authors discuss strategies for managing trade wars, which could impact equity markets and international relations.

articles.snippet: Learn how China's economy has evolved in recent years, ranging from its manufacturing exports sector to the massive housing boom and bust and more, with one of PIIE's top China experts, Senior Fellow Tianlei Huang. What can we learn from China's changing consumption and investment patterns? How did the housing market become so important to China's economy and what does its downfall mean moving forward? Huang explains all of this and more to host Anjali V. Bhatt, drawing on research from his forthcoming book, Detox: China's Fiscal Reckoning in the Shadow of the Housing Bust. HOST Anjali V.…

articles.title: The Fertilizer Shock That Could Trigger a Global Food Crisis
articles.snippet: Following the United States-Israeli attack on Iran and the ongoing war, trade has been severely disrupted between Asia and Europe. According to the International Energy Agency (IEA), the world is currently facing the worst oil disruption in history. The energy shortages felt over the last two and a half months have had a knock-on effect on other sectors, particularly on the fertiliser industry, leaving farmers around the globe without the inputs they need for their crops to grow, which could lead to severe food shortages in the months ahead. …
articles.title_it: Lo shock dei fertilizzanti potrebbe scatenare una crisi alimentare globale
articles.title_en: The Fertilizer Shock That Could Trigger a Global Food Crisis
articles.summary_it: La crisi dei fertilizzanti, legata alla guerra in Ucraina e in Medio Oriente, potrebbe portare a una crisi alimentare globale.
articles.summary_en: The fertilizer crisis, linked to the war in Ukraine and the Middle East, could lead to a global food crisis.

articles.title: Beijing’s Silence Is Fueling the Hormuz Crisis
articles.snippet: Even though the Xi–Trump summit in Beijing was supposed to project stability, the outcome was clearly the opposite. In real terms, the meeting could ultimately be remembered as the moment the world began to understand that there is no viable great-power strategy to contain the Iran war or to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The latter will have a long-lasting, debilitating effect on the stability of global shipping and energy markets. Even when taking into account all the choreography, ceremonial handshakes, and triumphant statements, the meeting…
